lint_etiquette.assessment: Lint handling was generally constructive: the initial crowding warnings were fixed by spacing the stores, and later label, covered-content, and broken-edge findings were addressed through label movement, segment shifts, reroutes, or removal of problematic labels. Five error-severity lint emissions appeared during routing, but no identical lint was re-fired for more than three consecutive turns without a strategy change, so this was not a lint fight. The final mutating operation reported the remaining warning resolved. No warnings were knowingly committed open, so there was no warning override requiring a verbatim summary reason.

The operation volume was proportionate to a large ten-section architecture diagram. There were no add-delete-rebuild cycles or repeated NO-OPs. The three consecutive malformed `look` attempts were avoidable validation thrash, but they did not cause abandonment or budget pressure.
